change_class: NEW PUBLIC SURFACE — a second channel for an aggregate already published; no new field, no new number
change_note: The track record becomes callable as a TOOL. Three live tool descriptions (get_trade_call, get_trade_signal, get_market_regime) cite performance://signal-performance as the evidence behind their trust claim, and a harness that bridges tools only cannot open a resource URI — DeepSeek Harness says so verbatim in packages/mcp/mcp-client/README.md: 'Tools are the only bridged MCP capability — Resources and Prompts have no harness consumer mechanism and are deferred.' So the citation was a dead pointer in the one place the moat is supposed to be provable. This tool computes NOTHING: it reads the one producer (getSignalPerformance) and projects it through the one exported allow-list formatter (src/lib/public-performance-formatter.ts) that performance://signal-performance and GET /api/performance-public also call. Two code paths computing a win rate is how two different win rates ship. The full aggregate is ~1.1 MB (byExchange carries a per-asset breakdown per venue), which is unusable inside the very harness this tool exists for, so the DEFAULT response is the compact head and byAsset / byExchange / recentSignals are opt-in via `include`. `include` widens the SECTIONS returned; it never widens the ROWS disclosed.
forbidden_keys_note: `equities` is forbidden HERE and was simultaneously REMOVED from performance://signal-performance by this wave. It is absent from audits/api-performance-public-shape-snapshot-2026-07-15.json's allowed_keys, and equities are under the standing public-copy HOLD that keeps both equity tools publicListing:false — so a second public channel carrying it would have widened a held disclosure. The formatter cannot emit it: the output object is built by naming permitted keys, never by spreading the producer's value.

row_allow_list.venues: byExchange is restricted to listVenues('promoted') INTERSECT getActivePromotedVenueIds() — the fail-CLOSED DB read narrowed by the retired-venue subtraction. Measured 2026-08-28 that is 14 ids; BITMART and EDGEX are `retired` and WEEX is `shadow`, and none of the three may appear. An unreadable or empty venues table yields NO per-venue rows, never all of them (the SV-02 contract from OPS-AUDIT-REMEDIATION-MED-W1).
row_allow_list.timeframes: Shadow timeframes (1m, 3m) are stripped from byTimeframe — and from each admitted venue's nested byTimeframe — unless named in SHADOW_REVEAL_TIMEFRAMES. Prod reveals 3m only, so 1m must not appear.
row_allow_list.enforcement: Allow-list BY CONSTRUCTION in src/lib/public-performance-formatter.ts: the output object is built by naming permitted keys, so a field added to PerformanceStats cannot leak through and a newly-shadowed venue is excluded with no code edit.

error_contract: The tool REFUSES in-band (structured payload + isError:true), it never throws: (a) INVALID_INCLUDE when `include` names a section outside the literal union — the payload lists allowed_sections and a suggested_include; (b) VENUE_BREAKDOWN_UNAVAILABLE when byExchange was explicitly requested and the venue allow-list is empty, which distinguishes 'registry unreadable' from 'no venues listed' instead of serving an ambiguous {}. A default call (no include) never hits either branch. Unexpected errors fall through to index.ts toolErrorContent.

cache_contract.description: Inherits the producer's bucket-keyed rolling aggregate cache (getPerformanceStatsAsync). The tool adds no cache of its own, so tool and resource observe the same generation. The venue allow-list inherits venue-store's retired-set TTL cache.
cache_contract.per_caller_variance: None. The response carries no license-derived or per-caller field; `_algovault` is the static public CTA block plus the tool name, package version and the echoed include list.

consumers: MCP clients that bridge tools only (DeepSeek Harness @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client, Codex-style harnesses)
GET /capabilities projection (registry-derived; name + description + channels + quota)
drift_check_command: curl -s -X POST https://api.algovault.com/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_track_record","arguments":{}}}' --max-time 30 | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | head -1 | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.loads(json.load(sys.stdin)['result']['content'][0]['text']); ALLOW=['totalCalls','period','overall','byCallType','byTimeframe','byTier','methodology','_algovault']; assert sorted(d.keys())==sorted(ALLOW), 'DEFAULT-KEY DRIFT: '+str(sorted(d.keys())); blob=json.dumps(d); assert all(k not in blob for k in ['equities','outcome_return_pct','outcome_price','pfe_return_pct','mae_return_pct']), 'FORBIDDEN KEY LEAK'; print('shape OK, tool', d['_algovault']['tool'])"

anchors_at_capture.note: The ~64x size ratio between the default head and the fully-included response is the reason `include` exists: byExchange alone is ~466 KB because it carries a per-asset breakdown for every venue. A key-set change, a forbidden-key leak, or a per-venue row for a non-promoted venue is the drift signal.
anchors_at_capture.bytes_measured_note: Measured on the LIVE tool post-deploy 2026-08-29, not estimated. The pre-deploy figure written here was 18000 for the default response and was WRONG by ~2x: byTier carries a full `assets[]` ticker array per tier, which the compact head keeps. The ratio that justifies `include` is unchanged and is the point — 36 KB default vs 1.09 MB fully included, ~30x.
anchors_at_capture.field_identity_note: Live post-deploy: the fully-included tool response minus `_algovault` is field-identical to `performance://signal-performance` across 41,843 JSON paths, zero differences. Scalar VALUES drift by the signals recorded between the two calls (measured: totalCalls 521694 vs 521693) — identity is asserted on the path set, never on values across two points in a live stream.
